rules.title: No Any
rules.check: any is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN. Use unknown if necessary.

rules.title: No Type Assertions
rules.check: Avoid as Type assertions. They hide bugs. Use type guards instead.
rules.bad_example: const user = response as User; // If response is wrong, this crashes later

rules.title: Readonly by Default
rules.check: Prefer readonly properties to prevent mutation bugs.

rules.title: Branded Types
rules.check: Use "Branded Types" for IDs to prevent mixing them.
rules.good_example:
type UserId = string & { __brand: 'UserId' };
type OrderId = string & { __brand: 'OrderId' };

rules.title: Discriminated Unions
rules.check: Use Discriminated Unions for state management.
rules.bad_example: interface State { isLoading: boolean; error?: string; data?: any; }

rules.title: Strict Null Checks
rules.check: strictNullChecks MUST be enabled. Handle null/undefined.
rules.bad_example: user.profile.name // Crash if profile is undefined

rules.title: Interface Over Type Alias
rules.check: Use interface for Objects, type for Unions.

rules.title: Generic Constraints
rules.bad_example: function getLength<T>(arg: T) { return arg.length; } // Error
rules.good_example: function getLength<T extends { length: number }>(arg: T) { return arg.length; }

rules.title: Utility Types
rules.bad_example: interface PartialUser { name?: string; age?: number; } // Duplicate definition

rules.title: Return Type Annotations
rules.check: Functions MUST have explicit return types.

rules.title: Template Literal Types
rules.check: Use template literal types for string patterns (routes, IDs, events).

rules.title: Const Type Parameters
rules.check: Use const type parameters for literal inference in generic functions.
rules.bad_example:
function createRoute<T extends string>(path: T) { return { path }; }
const route = createRoute("/users"); // type: { path: string }
rules.good_example:
function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T) { return { path }; }
const route = createRoute("/users"); // type: { path: "/users" }

rules.title: Satisfies Operator
rules.check: Use satisfies to validate types without widening. Prefer over as const when validating shape.

rules.title: No Object/Function Types
rules.check: Never use Object, Function, {} as types. Use specific shapes or unknown.

rules.title: Zod Schema for Runtime Validation
rules.check: External data (API responses, form inputs) SHOULD use Zod schemas for runtime validation.
rules.rationale: TypeScript types disappear at runtime. Zod provides runtime validation with type inference, catching invalid data at system boundaries.

rules.title: Infer Types from Schemas
rules.check: When using Zod, types SHOULD be inferred from schemas rather than manually duplicated.
rules.rationale: Inferring types from schemas ensures runtime validation and compile-time types stay in sync. Manual duplication leads to drift.
